_source: Written for the club and committed here because the articles table cannot be written from a developer machine: anonymous INSERT on `articles` is refused by row-level security (42501), which is the security posture working as designed. Only an admin session in Control panel -> News can create one.
_note:
THE SAME DEVICE AS fixtures-2627.json, for the same reason. A piece the club wants published today should not wait on somebody being at a laptop with a login. Each entry LOSES to a stored row with the same slug, so the moment this article is entered in the panel the database copy wins and this one disappears from the build. It cannot produce a duplicate.

The shape is the shape the panel writes: the whole body lives in `lede`, which is how all five existing articles are stored. Anything the panel would store and this file omits simply is not set.
_replaceWhen: Delete an entry once the same article exists in the Supabase `articles` table. Nothing breaks if that is forgotten, because the stored row already wins; the file just carries a copy nobody reads.

data.lede:
This morning, the waiting ends.

After a summer of preparation, rebuilding and anticipation, competitive football returns for Sue’s Angels FC today.

At 11:00, Three Little Birds FC will visit The Reeves Sports Club as the Angels begin their 2026/27 Southern Sunday Football League campaign.

It will be the club’s first fixture in League Eight, the opening match of its second competitive season and the next step in a journey that has already created unforgettable memories.

Twelve months ago, Sue’s Angels were preparing to play their first competitive match as a newly formed football club.

There was no previous campaign to look back on. There was no established league record, no reputation and no guarantee of what the group could achieve.

There was simply a collection of players, coaches, friends and volunteers brought together by football and by a shared commitment to honour the memory of Susan Anne Martin.

By the end of that first season, the Angels had made history.

Today, after an extraordinary debut campaign, they begin again.

## A first season that will never be forgotten

Sue’s Angels entered League Ten at the beginning of the 2025/26 season with ambition, belief and something greater than football behind the badge.

The team had been assembled, the identity of the club had been established and the purpose was clear. What remained unknown was how quickly everything would come together on the pitch.

The answer arrived almost immediately.

The Angels won their opening league fixture and continued winning until every league match had been completed.

Eighteen matches produced eighteen victories.

The team collected the maximum 54 points, finished as unbeaten League Ten champions and secured promotion with a perfect record.

**Played 18. Won 18. Fifty-four points from a possible 54.**

Some victories came through dominant attacking displays. Others required patience, discipline and the ability to find a way through difficult moments.

The Angels had to win in different conditions, at different venues and against opponents with different approaches. They had to manage expectations as their winning run grew and respond to the increasing determination of every team that wanted to be the first to take points from them.

As the season progressed, Sue’s Angels went from being an unknown new club to the team everybody wanted to stop.

The pressure increased, but the results continued.

The league title was secured before the final fixture, yet the group refused to allow its standards to fall. Once the championship had been won, the objective became even greater.

The players wanted to complete the entire campaign without dropping a single league point.

They achieved it.

The perfect record was not built in one afternoon. It was created through months of consistency, commitment and collective responsibility.

Different players stepped forward at different moments. Goals came from across the squad, while the defensive unit repeatedly provided the platform for the team to perform with confidence.

The season belonged to everyone who represented the badge.

## The numbers behind the achievement

The scale of the Angels’ opening campaign extended far beyond the final League Ten table.

Across all competitive competitions, Sue’s Angels played 33 matches.

They won 29, drew once and lost only three.

The team scored 137 goals and conceded just 25.

Those numbers reflected the balance within the group.

The Angels could attack with pace, create chances in different ways and punish opponents when matches began to open up. At the other end, the team defended with discipline and produced a series of clean sheets throughout the campaign.

The club’s biggest competitive victory was a 12-0 win away to Balham Bteckerz in League Ten.

There were other emphatic results, including nine and ten-goal victories during the closing stages of the league campaign. But the season was not defined only by comfortable scorelines.

There were narrow wins, physical contests and matches in which the Angels had to remain patient.

There were days when the football flowed and others when character mattered more than performance.

Those difficult victories played an equally important role in the championship. They showed that the team could continue finding answers when an opponent disrupted its rhythm or when the match did not unfold as expected.

That resilience will be needed again at the higher level.

## A debut season filled with cup memories

The Angels’ first year also included memorable cup journeys.

Alongside the perfect league campaign, Sue’s Angels competed against teams from different levels and tested themselves in unfamiliar environments.

The club progressed through several rounds of cup competition and reached the final of the Dylan Rigobert Trophy.

For a team completing its first season, reaching a final represented another significant achievement.

The final ended in a 3-0 defeat against FC Porto of London. It was a disappointing result on the day, but it did not erase the progress required to reach that stage.

The occasion gave the players experience of preparing for a final, competing under greater pressure and representing the club on another important platform.

It also provided a reminder that progress does not remove the possibility of disappointment.

Success must be earned repeatedly. There will always be another opponent, another challenge and another standard to reach.

The Angels ended their first campaign with a league championship, a perfect record and the experience of competing in a cup final.

Together, those achievements created the foundation for what begins this morning.

## More than a trophy

Winning League Ten did not simply add the first piece of silverware to the club’s history.

It earned Sue’s Angels a two-division rise.

The Angels will compete in League Eight throughout the 2026/27 season, moving beyond League Nine and entering a division filled with new opponents and greater challenges.

That rise is recognition of everything the team achieved during its debut campaign.

It is also a demand to improve.

The margins are likely to become smaller. Mistakes will be punished more regularly and matches may remain competitive for longer.

Opponents will arrive with experience, quality and ambitions of their own. There will be moments when the Angels cannot dominate possession or create chances as freely as they did last season.

The team will need to remain composed when games become tight and resilient when momentum moves in the opposite direction.

Last season created belief.

This season will test how strong that belief has become.

## The next level begins now

Moving from League Ten to League Eight is an important moment in the club’s development.

It gives Sue’s Angels an opportunity to discover how their football compares against stronger and more established opposition.

The players have earned the right to test themselves at this level.

However, promotion does not guarantee that the next stage will be comfortable.

The title, the perfect record and the goals scored during 2025/26 offer no advantage once the opening whistle is blown this morning.

They provide confidence and experience, but they cannot win a tackle, defend a cross or finish an opportunity.

Everything must be earned again.

The challenge is not to reproduce every scoreline from last season. It is to carry forward the standards that made those results possible.

The work rate.

The discipline.

The togetherness.

The willingness to take responsibility when the match becomes difficult.

Those qualities must travel with the team into League Eight.

## Eight opponents stand in the way

Sue’s Angels will face a new group of teams during the 2026/27 campaign.

Barnes Stormers, Bristol City (London) Supporters, Brockwell Violets, Haydons Park, Junction Elite, Pure Football, Three Little Birds and TSM Rovers will provide the opposition across the season.

Some of those clubs will be familiar from cup competitions and previous fixtures outside the league. Others will present completely new challenges.

Every team will bring its own identity.

There will be opponents who look to control possession, teams prepared to defend before attacking quickly, and sides determined to turn matches into physical battles.

The Angels will need to recognise those differences and adapt.

Winning a league requires more than one way of playing.

The team must be able to control matches when the opportunity is there, remain patient when space is limited and compete when the quality of football alone is not enough.

There will be mornings when everything works and others when the performance feels difficult from the opening minutes.

The response in those moments will help determine what Sue’s Angels can achieve in League Eight.

## Three Little Birds arrive at The Reeves

The first challenge comes from Three Little Birds FC.

Like Sue’s Angels, this morning’s visitors are entering unfamiliar surroundings and beginning a new chapter.

Three Little Birds competed in the Metropolitan Sunday Football League last season before moving across to the Southern Sunday Football League for 2026/27.

They finished eighth in an eight-team division, recording three victories and two draws from 21 league matches.

Their final position suggests they endured a difficult campaign, particularly during the closing stages of the season.

However, the league table does not tell the complete story of what they are capable of producing.

Three Little Birds demonstrated their attacking threat in several convincing victories.

Their campaign included emphatic 5-1 and 5-0 wins at home, alongside impressive 5-1 and 5-2 victories away from home.

Those performances show that the visitors are capable of scoring heavily when given space, confidence and momentum.

The Angels must ensure they are not allowed to find any of those things easily this morning.

## A fresh start for the visitors

Three Little Birds’ move into a new competition offers them the opportunity to reset.

Players may have arrived during the summer. Previous weaknesses may have been addressed and the squad beginning today’s match may look very different from the one that completed last season.

A change of league can create fresh energy around a club.

It removes the weight of previous results and gives every player the opportunity to begin with a clean record.

Three Little Birds will travel to The Reeves knowing that victory over last season’s unbeaten League Ten champions would provide the perfect introduction to their new competition.

That motivation makes them dangerous.

Sue’s Angels cannot approach the fixture believing that last season’s records will determine what happens today.

The two clubs competed in different leagues, faced different opponents and experienced different circumstances.

Neither previous table will be present on the pitch this morning.

**At 11:00, the score will be 0-0.**

## No history and no assumptions

There is no established rivalry between Sue’s Angels and Three Little Birds.

There is no previous meeting to analyse and no direct result that can be used to measure one side against the other.

That uncertainty adds another layer to the opening fixture.

The Angels will not know exactly how Three Little Birds intend to approach the match.

The visitors may press aggressively from the opening whistle. They may choose to defend in a compact shape and attack on the counter. They may look to make the contest physical and prevent the Angels from settling into their rhythm.

Sue’s Angels will need to read the game quickly.

They must recognise the spaces available, understand where the danger is coming from and make the necessary adjustments throughout the match.

That requires communication, concentration and patience.

Opening-day energy can sometimes make teams rush their decisions. The Angels must play with intensity without losing control.

They must respect the opponent without allowing that respect to weaken their confidence.

The objective is to impose their own standards while remaining prepared for whatever challenge Three Little Birds present.

## A summer of preparation

The period between seasons has given Sue’s Angels time to prepare for the step into League Eight.

Pre-season has included a varied schedule designed to provide minutes, test combinations and challenge the group against opponents with different qualities.

The results have been mixed.

There have been victories, a draw and defeats.

There have been encouraging performances, alongside difficult periods that exposed areas in which the team needed to improve.

That is the purpose of pre-season.

It is not there to extend an unbeaten record or create the appearance of perfection.

It exists to prepare players for competitive football.

The summer fixtures have allowed members of the squad to rebuild fitness, develop partnerships and gain experience against teams capable of punishing mistakes.

The Angels have experienced matches in which they controlled long periods of play and others in which they were forced to defend, recover and find different solutions.

Those challenges should prove valuable.

A team learns little when every match is comfortable.

It learns much more when the game forces players to communicate, solve problems and remain together when momentum moves against them.

The results will not count towards the League Eight table.

The lessons must.

## Preparation must now become performance

This morning is where the experimentation ends.

There are points available.

The intensity will rise, every challenge will carry greater importance and each moment can influence the outcome.

Sue’s Angels must transfer the work completed during the summer into a competitive performance.

The opening stages will be particularly important.

Both sides will arrive with energy and a desire to establish control. The Angels will need to begin sharply, compete for second balls and avoid giving the visitors encouragement through unnecessary mistakes.

Patience will also matter.

The first goal may not arrive immediately. The match may require the team to keep moving the ball, continue creating opportunities and trust the process rather than forcing the final pass.

If Three Little Birds start strongly, the Angels must remain composed.

If Sue’s Angels take control, they must use that control properly.

League football rewards teams capable of managing every phase of a match, not only the moments when they are playing well.

## The challenge of the second season

A club’s second season presents a different psychological test from its first.

When Sue’s Angels entered League Ten last year, they were unknown.

There were no achievements for opponents to discuss and no title-winning record for anybody to target.

That has changed.

Sue’s Angels begin 2026/27 as unbeaten champions.

Every opponent will know that the team won all 18 of its league fixtures last season. Every club will see the Angels as a side worth beating.

The badge now carries a reputation that did not exist twelve months ago.

That attention should be treated as a privilege.

It has been earned through performance.

But reputation alone will not protect the Angels when matches become difficult.

The players must continue doing the work that created the reputation in the first place.

Training must remain competitive. Standards must continue to be enforced and every member of the squad must remain accountable to the group.

The championship cannot be allowed to create complacency.

Winning last season does not make the Angels entitled to success this season.

If anything, the standards must become higher.

## From champions to challengers

Sue’s Angels will always be the 2025/26 League Ten champions.

That title is part of the club’s history and cannot be taken away.

But the players must enter League Eight as challengers.

This season is not about protecting an unbeaten record that belongs to a different division.

It is about pursuing the next level with the same hunger that existed before the first match in the club’s history.

There should be confidence in what the group has achieved, but there can be no assumption that another perfect campaign will follow.

League Eight will contain difficult mornings.

There will be matches when the Angels are forced to defend for longer than they would like. There will be occasions when chances are missed, decisions go against them or the opposition performs at a high level.

There may be setbacks.

The strongest teams are not those that avoid every difficult moment. They are the teams capable of responding when those moments arrive.

The ability to respond was present throughout the Angels’ first season.

It will become even more important during their second.

## Opportunities across the squad

A new campaign brings new opportunities.

Every player begins the season with the chance to influence what comes next.

The individuals who played central roles in last season’s success will want to continue setting the standard. Those who received fewer minutes will have another opportunity to establish themselves.

New additions can bring different qualities and increase competition across the squad.

That internal competition will be important.

A long season cannot be carried by eleven players.

Availability will change. Injuries and suspensions may arrive. Form will rise and fall, and different fixtures will require different solutions.

Every member of the squad must remain ready.

The strength of Sue’s Angels during their first campaign came from the collective. Goals, assists, defensive contributions and important moments arrived from throughout the team.

That same depth will be required in League Eight.

This morning represents the first opportunity for the group to show how it has developed.

## The importance of beginning at home

Starting the season at The Reeves Sports Club gives the Angels an opportunity to take their first League Eight step in familiar surroundings.

The Reeves has become the club’s home.

It is where the players, coaches, families, friends and supporters have gathered to share the journey.

It has witnessed victories, goals and the gradual development of a new football club into an unbeaten league champion.

This morning, it will host another important moment.

Home advantage is created by more than familiarity with the pitch.

It comes from the energy around the ground, the encouragement from the touchline and the feeling that the entire club is moving in the same direction.

A strong presence beside the pitch can lift the team during difficult periods and help create momentum when the Angels are on top.

That support will matter throughout the season.

League Eight will test the group in new ways, and the connection between the players and everyone surrounding the club will remain important.

Sue’s Angels have never been built around the eleven players on the pitch alone.

The progress has always been collective.

## Still built in her name

Whatever changes on the pitch, the purpose behind Sue’s Angels remains unchanged.

The club was founded in memory of Susan Anne Martin and continues to play for sepsis awareness.

That purpose is not simply a message added to the team.

It is the foundation upon which the club was created.

Every match provides another opportunity to carry Susan’s name forward and encourage more people to understand the warning signs of sepsis.

The football matters.

The results matter.

The ambition to compete, improve and win remains strong.

But the badge represents something deeper than a league position or a final score.

It represents memory, family, friendship and the determination to create something positive that can continue growing.

Promotion provides a bigger platform for that purpose.

As the club moves through the divisions and faces new opponents, more players, supporters and communities will discover what Sue’s Angels represents.

Every fixture allows the message to reach somebody new.

Every person who wears the shirt becomes part of carrying that message.

The team plays in her name.

The players compete for one another.

The club continues for everyone connected to its story.

That will remain true regardless of the division, the opposition or the result.

## The standard remains the same

The surroundings will be familiar this morning.

The players will enter the same dressing room, step onto the same home pitch and see many of the same faces beside the touchline.

But almost everything else will feel different.

The league is new.

The opponent is new.

The pressure is different and the challenge is greater.

That is exactly what the Angels earned.

The expectation is not perfection.

It is commitment.

Compete for every ball.

Communicate through every phase of the match.

Support one another when mistakes happen.

Remain disciplined when the game becomes difficult.

Play with confidence when opportunities appear.

Represent the name on the shirt properly from the first whistle until the last.

Those are the standards that created last season’s success.

They must remain at the centre of everything the team does next.

## Setting the tone for the season

The opening fixture will not decide where either team finishes in May.

There will be many more matches, challenges and opportunities to follow.

However, the first performance can establish the tone.

Sue’s Angels will want to show from the opening minutes that they are prepared to compete at the higher level.

That does not mean the team must play the perfect match.

It means displaying the behaviours that will be required throughout the campaign.

Intensity without recklessness.

Confidence without complacency.

Ambition without losing discipline.

Togetherness when the match becomes uncomfortable.

Three points would provide the ideal beginning, but the performance must also demonstrate that the team understands the challenge ahead.

The Angels are not entering League Eight to admire the level.

They are entering it to compete.

## The first step of a longer journey

One match will never define an entire season.

A victory today would provide the perfect start, but it would still represent only the first step.

A difficult result would not decide what follows either.

A league campaign is built over months.

It requires consistency when energy is high and discipline when the weather changes, availability becomes difficult and the excitement of the opening weeks has faded.

It requires players to remain connected through victories and disappointments.

The Angels demonstrated those qualities last season.

Now they must reproduce them in a stronger division.

Today matters because it provides the first opportunity to collect points and make an impression.

But the club’s ambition extends far beyond one morning.

Sue’s Angels want to prove that the success of their debut season was not an isolated achievement.

The club wants to continue developing, competing and building something capable of lasting.

The League Ten trophy is part of the foundation.

Today, another level begins to be built on top of it.

## Today, the next chapter begins

This morning, Sue’s Angels will walk onto the pitch as unbeaten League Ten champions.

They will leave it having completed their first match in League Eight.

Between those two moments will be 90 minutes of competitive football against an opponent beginning a new journey of its own.

Three Little Birds will arrive looking to make an immediate impact in the Southern Sunday Football League.

Sue’s Angels will be determined to establish themselves at the higher level and begin the new season strongly in front of their home support.

Nothing is guaranteed.

That is what makes the opening day special.

The table is empty.

Every team begins on zero points and the possibilities remain open.

Last season has been written into the history of Sue’s Angels FC.

Today, the club begins writing what comes next.

## Be there for the beginning

Competitive football is back at The Reeves Sports Club.

Come down, stand alongside the club and support the Angels as they take their first step into League Eight.

Bring your voice.

Bring your support.

Be there when the next chapter begins.

**FIXTURE**

Sue’s Angels FC v Three Little Birds FC

**DATE**

Sunday 6 September 2026

**KICK-OFF**

11:00

**VENUE**

The Reeves Sports Club

**COMPETITION**

Southern Sunday Football League, League Eight

Last season, we created history.

Today, we begin again.

A new league. A greater challenge. The same badge. The same purpose.

**We go again.**

data.lede:
Sue’s Angels sit at the top of League Eight after winning their opening two matches, but the story of their start cannot be explained by the table alone.

The victories arrived in completely different ways.

On the opening day, the Angels defeated Three Little Birds 2–1.

It was a difficult match in which the opposition started strongly and created several opportunities. Munns made eight saves, while the Angels moved through three formations as they attempted to gain control and eventually protect their lead.

Lloyd and Dunkley scored the goals, but Sue’s Angels did not reach their expected level.

The performance left the players with two truths.

They had collected three points in their first League Eight fixture, but they also knew significant improvement would be required.

Seven days later, the response arrived.

Haydons Park were beaten 8–1 as the Angels produced the type of football that defined their strongest performances during the previous campaign.

The pressing was aggressive. Possession was moved with patience and purpose. The attacking players combined effectively, while Haydons Park were prevented from developing any sustained momentum.

Five goals before half-time placed the result beyond serious doubt.

By the final whistle, Owolana and Dunkley had completed hat-tricks. Burnett had converted a penalty, while Brumpton had registered his first competitive goal for the club.

The afternoon also welcomed Jimi back from retirement and introduced Cain and Churchill to competitive football with the Angels.

## More than six points

Sue’s Angels have six points from six, but the most encouraging aspect of the opening fortnight has been the variety within the victories.

The first required resilience and tactical flexibility.

The second demonstrated confidence, control and attacking quality.

Successful teams experience matches when their football does not flow. The ability to win those games is important. It becomes even more valuable when the players recognise their shortcomings and produce an immediate response.

That is what Sue’s Angels achieved.

The opening fixtures have also demonstrated the strength of the developing squad.

Summer arrivals have contributed immediately. Established players have maintained their influence. Returning players have provided experience, and two more members of the squad have now made their competitive debuts.

## The early League Eight picture

After two fixtures, Sue’s Angels have scored ten goals, conceded two and collected the maximum six points.

Their goal difference of plus eight placed them at the top of League Eight after Gameweek Two.

However, the position confirms that Sue’s Angels have adapted quickly following their two-division promotion.

Last season, the Angels won all 18 league fixtures and secured the League Ten title during their first year as a club.

The move into League Eight was always going to demand more. The opposition would be stronger, mistakes would carry a greater cost and the Angels would need to prove themselves again.

The opening-day victory showed that the team could find a way to win when below its best.

The victory over Haydons Park showed what could happen when the performance matched the ambition.

Two matches do not define a season.

They can establish its direction.

Sue’s Angels have made the perfect start. The challenge now is to continue setting the pace.

data.title: Angels drawn away to Peps All Stars in President's Cup
data.lede:
Sue’s Angels FC will travel to Peps All Stars in the first round of the Brian Howard President’s Cup.

The draw, completed on Wednesday 16 September, placed the Angels in Tie 2. A date and venue have yet to be confirmed by the Southern Sunday Football League.

!![Brian Howard President’s Cup first round: Peps All Stars v Sue’s Angels FC, Tie 2, date to be confirmed](/assets/articles/presidents-cup-first-round.jpg#1200x750)

## A first meeting

Peps All Stars are completely new opposition for Sue’s Angels.

The clubs have never met in the league, a cup competition or a friendly, leaving both sides without a previous result to study.

That unfamiliarity adds another dimension to the Angels’ first President’s Cup campaign. With no existing form line between the teams, preparation, discipline and the ability to understand the contest quickly will be essential.

## The route ahead

A total of 28 clubs entered the competition. Twenty-four will contest the first round, while Celtic Swans, Deportivo Los Toros, Pure FC 2.0 and Shepherds Tuesday received byes.

If the Angels overcome Peps All Stars, Celtic Swans will await them in the second round.

The quarter-final section contains Deportivo Los Toros, Balham and Clapham Albion and League Eight opponents Haydons Park. That creates the possibility of a reunion with the side beaten 8–1 at The Reeves, although both clubs must first progress through their earlier ties.

Possible semi-final opponents include Brockwell Violets, Three Little Birds, Sporting Club Catania, Hillside Blues, BPR, Pure Football 1st Team, Bristol City (London) Supporters and Larkhall City.

!![The Angels’ potential route: Peps All Stars away, followed by Celtic Swans and then one of several familiar league and cup opponents](/assets/articles/presidents-cup-route-wide.jpg#1400x660)

| Round | Tie | Possible opposition |
|---|---|---|
| First round | 2 | Peps All Stars, away |
| Second round | 20 | Celtic Swans |
| Quarter-final | 23 | Deportivo Los Toros, Haydons Park or Balham and Clapham Albion |
| Semi-final | 26 | One of eight clubs from the Angels’ half |
| Final | 27 | Winner of the opposite half |

League Eight rivals TSM Rovers, Junction Elite, Barnes Stormers and Old Freemen’s are all positioned in the opposite half. The Angels could only meet one of those clubs in the final.

## Experience to build upon

Sue’s Angels played 15 cup ties and won 11 during their first season.

Their longest run came in the Dylan Rigobert Trophy, where victories over Brockwell Violets, Larkhall City, Barnes Stormers and Hillside Blues earned the club a place in the final.

The Angels scored 21 goals and conceded only once across those four victories before losing 3–0 to FC Porto of London in the final.

That experience showed both sides of knockout football. The team demonstrated its ability to produce commanding performances, but also learned how quickly a cup journey can end.

The President’s Cup now offers another opportunity to compete for silverware and build upon an encouraging first-season record.

## League business comes first

Before attention turns fully towards Peps All Stars, the Angels face two important League Eight fixtures.

Sue’s Angels travel to Junction Elite on Sunday 20 September before welcoming Barnes Stormers to The Reeves the following weekend.

The Angels currently lead League Eight after opening the campaign with a hard-fought 2–1 victory over Three Little Birds and an emphatic 8–1 win against Haydons Park.

The date for the cup tie will be announced once confirmed by the league.

For now, the route is visible, but only the opening challenge matters.

Peps All Stars away.

On Sunday morning we play our first Brian Howard President's Cup tie, away to Peps All Stars at Dulwich Park.

Before kick-off we sat down with manager [Stephen Epathite](/coaches/stephen-epathite.html) to talk about the opening month, the cup final we lost last season, and what he wants from the side from the first whistle.

Press play above for the whole conversation. Everything he said is written out below it, and every timestamp takes you straight to that answer in the recording.

@[Stephen Epathite on the President's Cup tie](/assets/audio/stephen-presidents-cup.mp3#4:16|/assets/players/stephen-epathite-portrait.webp)

> 2:18 That sting is giving me fire to go and repair what happened last year.

?? 0:09 | Adapting to League Eight | Four games, four wins, and we have stepped up two divisions. What has impressed you most about how we have adapted to League Eight?

The consistency, and the transition from where we left off last season. All the credit goes to the players: they have carried on exactly as we ended last season. The mentality, the attitude, the hunger, the desire. And I still think we have not got started properly yet.

++[26/27]

?? 0:42 | Where he wants more | We have scored 20 goals in those four games. If there was one area you wanted improved, what would it be?

I am really happy so far with what they have done, and without over-criticising the team, I still think we have gears to go through. I still think we need to gel, and that there is more to come in terms of the football we want to play and the chemistry between the players.

If I am critical, clean sheets is probably the one area where I would say we need to keep more of them. And in front of goal, just be more ruthless with the chances we get. Overall, I am happy at the moment.

?? 1:32 | The cup final sting | We came close in the cup last season, reaching a final, but fell short. What does that experience give us this season?

There is definitely a sting from that cup final. I feel it, and I think some of the players feel it as well.

As a team we want to get back to the same final we were in last year. We want to get there. And if we do get the chance to get there, a lot of things will be done differently, from my point of view and from the players'.

It definitely stung. And that sting is giving me fire to go and repair what happened last year.

?? 2:28 | Preparing for Peps | Sunday is against Peps All Stars, a team we have never played. How do you prepare for a cup tie against opposition we are unfamiliar with?

I prepare for every game exactly the same. I treat every game as a big game. I do not write anybody off, and I do not have any less respect for a team a division below or a division above, top of the league or bottom of the league.

I have prepared every single team I have ever managed exactly the same. Every game is a big game and you have to treat it like that. If you want to progress, especially in cup matches, if you take your eye off the ball you can get a nice little surprise along the way.

?? 3:14 | From the first whistle | When we step onto the pitch, what is the one thing you will be demanding from the very first whistle?

The week off has been good. I know the group very well, and I think it was a good thing to keep them fresh and keep their minds ready, because we had a lot of games in pre-season and a fast start to the season.

So tomorrow, I expect, and I know, that the players will be at it from minute one. I want the intensity, the aggression and the consistency we had last season carried into this season. The main thing is to win.

## Sunday

Peps All Stars v Sue's Angels FC, Brian Howard President's Cup round one, Dulwich Park, 10:30.

There is no previous meeting between the two clubs, and no second chance in this competition.
data.title: What the manager wants to see at Dulwich Park
Four goals, a clean sheet, and no talk of the final
data.lede:
Sue's Angels came away from Dulwich Park with a 4-0 win over Peps All Stars and a place in round two of the Brian Howard President's Cup. Ade Owolana scored twice, Leon Burnett and Daniel McLane got the others, and Luke Munns kept the clean sheet his manager had asked for.

Afterwards we sat down with [Stephen Epathite](/coaches/stephen-epathite.html) at the ground.

Press play above for the whole conversation. Everything he said is written out below it, and every timestamp takes you straight to that answer in the recording.

@[Stephen Epathite after the win at Peps All Stars](/assets/audio/stephen-peps-reaction.mp3#5:12|/assets/players/stephen-epathite-portrait.webp)

> 3:28 If we start thinking final, and it is only round two, we will be out quicker than we know it.

?? 0:08 | Four and a clean sheet | Four goals, a clean sheet and a place in the next round. What is your overall assessment of the performance?

I am happy. Very happy with the win and with going through. We are in the draw for the next round of the other cup we want to win.

I do not think 4-0 reflected the game. If we had come away with five or six more, I think that would have been about right. Credit to Peps All Stars: they battled, and they made things difficult for us.

But the clean sheet is the thing. That was somewhere I wanted to get to, I wanted a clean sheet, and I am pleased we have won 4-0 and pleased the strikers have been in positions to score.

On another day, and without being disrespectful to Peps All Stars, they are really good guys and they battled. The crossbar and the post helped them out today, and so did our lack of ruthlessness in front of goal.

++[26/27]

?? 1:27 | Why the clean sheet comes first | Before the game you spoke about wanting intensity from the first whistle and about improving our defensive record. How pleased were you with the way we delivered on that?

A clean sheet. I am always grateful for a clean sheet. That is my number one priority in every game.

It gives you a nice base to work from. If you are able to keep a clean sheet, it shows the other team have not been good enough to score against you in ninety minutes.

And with the defenders we have got, and the number of them, and with the midfielders, that gives the attacking players a nice base to work off. Which is what they did today.

?? 2:07 | The front players | Ade has two more goals to his tally, with Leon Burnett and Daniel McLane also on the score sheet. What pleased you most about our attacking play?

When we moved the ball quickly we had some nice patterns of play. Little one-touch movements, getting the ball out wide quickly. I thought we looked really good and really effective.

I am happy with all the strikers we have got. I am pleased with Ade and the goals he is getting. LJ was fantastic today: his first touch and his hold-up play were excellent. And Charlie's ability to run and create his own chances, although he did not score today. On another day he gets five or six.

I am pleased that our front players are creating those chances for themselves, and other players as well. So I am really pleased with the attacking part, and with the defensive part as well.

?? 3:08 | Another cup run | We spoke before the game about the disappointment of last season's cup final. Now we have cleared the first hurdle, what is the key to putting together another strong run?

The key is what I said before. It is game by game. If we start thinking final, and it is only round two, we will be out quicker than we know it.

So again, it is a process. Game by game, minute by minute, match by match, each week as it comes. We will deal with whatever comes in that week and we will see where we get to.

?? 3:41 | Mousa Mountain next | We return to league football next week against the division's newcomers, Mousa Mountain, looking to make it five wins from five. What is your main focus as we prepare?

Mousa Mountain are a new team and they have not played a game yet. So in a way we are the test pilots. It is their first game. I do not know much about them, and I do not think the league knows much about them either, so the league will be watching and will probably gauge off the result how things might play out.

But we have to treat them as we treat every team. We have to make sure that we are on it, and make sure that we are ready. Winning this league is something we want to do, and I think we are in a position where we can.

They are unknown, so the league will be watching, and we are the first to play them. I think they will be up for it. We will be up for it. That should make for a good game.

## Next

**Update, 17 October.** The match this interview looks ahead to will not be played. Mousa Mountain FC have folded. Everything above was said before we knew, and it is left as it was said.

The President's Cup round two tie is at home to Celtic Swans FC, with the date still to be confirmed.

data.title: Sunday is off. Here is where it leaves us
data.lede:
Sunday is off. Mousa Mountain FC have folded, the league told us on Saturday evening, and the League Eight match we were due to play at The Reeves on 18 October will not happen. It is never good news when a club goes under and we wish everybody there well.

So this piece is about us: where that leaves the season, the table and the next time we play.

## Five from five, and nothing to play on Sunday

We have won every match we have played this season. Twenty-four scored, three conceded, two clean sheets, and the only side in League Eight with a perfect record alongside Brockwell Violets.

!![Sue’s Angels in 26/27 so far: five played, five won, 24 scored, three conceded, with every result listed](/assets/articles/season-so-far-five-from-five.jpg#1200x750)

The run has not been one sort of win either. Three Little Birds took us to the wire on the opening day and Luke made eight saves to see it out. Haydons Park and Barnes Stormers were swept away at home. Junction Elite and Peps All Stars were won away from The Reeves without conceding. Different afternoons, same three points.

That is the form a free Sunday now interrupts.

## No points, and no change

**We have not been awarded any points**, and nobody else has either. The league has now confirmed that Mousa Mountain come out of League Eight altogether, so the division is nine clubs and the fixtures against them will not be replayed or awarded.

Our position does not move. The table reads the same at the top as it did before any of this:

| Club | P | W | D | L | GF | GA | GD | Pts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sue's Angels FC | 4 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 20 | 3 | 17 | 12 |
| Brockwell Violets | 4 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 10 | 3 | 7 | 12 |
| TSM Rovers | 3 | 2 | 0 | 1 | 11 | 5 | 6 | 6 |
| Three Little Birds | 3 | 2 | 0 | 1 | 8 | 5 | 3 | 6 |
| Bristol City (London) | 4 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 6 | 10 | -4 | 4 |
| Haydons Park | 3 | 1 | 0 | 2 | 7 | 13 | -6 | 3 |
| Junction Elite | 4 | 1 | 0 | 3 | 6 | 12 | -6 | 3 |
| Pure Football 1st | 3 | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 9 | -6 | 1 |
| Barnes Stormers | 4 | 0 | 0 | 4 | 3 | 14 | -11 | 0 |

* Mousa Mountain FC folded on 17 October 2026 and were removed from League Eight by the league. Their fixture at The Reeves on Sunday 18 October was not played, and no points were awarded.

Twelve points each at the top, and seventeen goals of difference against seven. That is the whole margin between us and Brockwell Violets, and it is the reason the 8-1 and the 7-1 matter as much as the 2-1 did.

One practical thing follows from nine clubs: there are fewer league games to play than the season started with, so there are fewer chances to make that difference up, for us and for everybody chasing.

## What comes next, and what is still to be confirmed

**We play again on Sunday 25 October.** The league has confirmed the Marcus Lipton tie: away at Juizo FC, 10:30, on pitch 6 at Clapham Common. The President’s Cup tie is drawn and still waiting on a date, and no further League Eight fixtures have been published.

- **Marcus Lipton Cup, first round** · Juizo FC, away at Clapham Common · Sunday 25 October, 10:30
- **President’s Cup, second round** · Celtic Swans FC, at The Reeves · date to be confirmed
- **League Eight** · no further fixtures published yet

Both are against clubs from higher up. The league runs eleven tiers and we are in the ninth of them. **Celtic Swans are in League Seven**, the division directly above ours. **Juizo FC are in League Four**, with League Five, Six and Seven between them and us.

### The President’s Cup tie

We earned it at Dulwich Park on 11 October, where Ade scored twice, LJ and Dan got the others and Luke kept a second clean sheet in three.

!![Brian Howard President’s Cup, second round: Sue’s Angels FC v Celtic Swans FC at The Reeves, with our route either side of it](/assets/articles/presidents-cup-round-two-celtic-swans.jpg#1200x750)

We have never played Celtic Swans: no league match, no cup tie, no friendly, nothing in the archive with their name on it. They were one of four clubs given a bye past the first round, so they come into it fresh while we have already had to win one. The tie is at The Reeves, which the league’s bracket decides rather than a toss-up.

Win it and the quarter-final is tie 23, against Deportivo Los Toros or Balham and Clapham Albion. It was three clubs when this was written: Haydons Park, the side we beat 8-1 here in September, went out of the cup 0-6 to Balham and Clapham Albion on 18 October. We have played neither of the two left.

### The Marcus Lipton tie

The other is a first-round tie away at **Juizo FC**, four divisions up. We have never played them either.

!![Supreme Trophies Marcus Lipton Cup, first round: Juizo FC v Sue’s Angels FC, with the route and last season’s run beside it](/assets/articles/marcus-lipton-first-round-juizo.jpg#1200x750)

It is the biggest draw we are in: 106 ties in all, 44 of them in the first round. Win this one and the second round is tie 51, away to Mala Vida FC or St Matthew’s Project.

That first name will ring a bell. Mala Vida are how this cup started for us last season, beaten 2-1 away in the first round, before Argentina FC’s first team put us out 0-2 in the second. Getting past Juizo would put the same round in front of us, and possibly the same opponent.

## What happens now

Nothing on 18 October. There was no match at The Reeves and nothing to turn up for.

The Sunday after is Clapham Common, and Juizo FC of League Four. The aim has not moved: keep the run going, stay at the top, and go further in these cups than we managed in the last one. As soon as the league puts a date on the President’s Cup tie, or publishes the next round of league fixtures, it will be posted here first.

data.title: We play again on Sunday, four divisions up
data.lede:
We have a match again. The league has confirmed our Marcus Lipton Cup first round tie: away at **Juizo FC**, 10:30 on Sunday 25 October, on pitch 6 at Clapham Common.

It is our first match in a fortnight, and the biggest step up we have taken all season.

## Five from five, and two Sundays without a game

Nothing has gone wrong. We have simply not had a match.

The last league game was Barnes Stormers on 27 September. The round on 4 October did not involve us. We won the President’s Cup tie at Peps All Stars on 11 October, and the following Sunday was taken off us when Mousa Mountain folded.

!![Sue’s Angels FC in 26/27 so far: five played, five won, 24 scored, 3 conceded, two clean sheets](/assets/articles/season-so-far-five-from-five.jpg#1200x750)

So the record stands where it did a fortnight ago: five competitive matches, five wins, 24 scored and 3 conceded. Ade Owolana has 9 of those goals and Charlie Dunkley 7. We are top of League Eight with four wins from four.

## Four divisions up

Juizo FC play in **League Four**. We are in League Eight. League Five, Six and Seven sit between us, and this league runs eleven tiers in all.

We have never played them. No league match, no cup tie, no friendly, nothing in the archive with their name on it, which means there is nothing here to tell you about how they play. Sunday is the first time anybody at this club sees them.

!![Supreme Trophies Marcus Lipton Cup, first round: Juizo FC v Sue’s Angels FC, Sunday 25 October at Clapham Common, with the route and last season’s run beside it](/assets/articles/marcus-lipton-first-round-juizo.jpg#1200x750)

A cup draw does not care about divisions, and the only thing four of them between two clubs guarantees is that nobody is expecting much of us. That is a reasonable place to start.

## A year to the week

This is the same cup that gave us our longest run last season, and almost the same weekend.

On 26 October 2025 we won 2-1 away at Mala Vida FC in the first round. On 30 November we went out 0-2 at Argentina FC’s first team in the second.

Win on Sunday and the second round is tie 51, away to **Mala Vida FC or St Matthew’s Project**. So getting through would put us back in the same round we reached last year, possibly against the same club we beat to get there.

It is the biggest draw we are in: 106 ties in all, and 44 clubs meet in the first round alone. Ours is tie 2.

## The other one is still waiting

The President’s Cup second round against **Celtic Swans FC** is drawn, it is at The Reeves, and the league has not yet put a date on it. No further League Eight fixtures have been published either. Both go up here as soon as they land.

## Where and when

- **Sunday 25 October, 10:30**
- **Clapham Common, pitch 6**
- Supreme Trophies Marcus Lipton Cup, first round
- Juizo FC v Sue’s Angels FC

The clocks go back that morning, so it is a genuine hour in hand rather than a lost one. Come down if you are near: it is a public common, it is free, and an away end of any size makes a difference at this level.

data.title: Happy and frustrated at the same time
data.lede:
Sue's Angels went out of the Supreme Trophies Marcus Lipton Cup on Sunday morning, beaten 4-3 on penalties by Juizo FC at Clapham Common after ninety goalless minutes against a side four divisions above us. [Luke Munns](/players/luke-munns.html) kept the clean sheet his manager had asked for. The goal at the other end never came.

Afterwards we spoke to [Stephen Epathite](/coaches/stephen-epathite.html).

Press play above for the whole conversation. Everything he said is written out below it, and every timestamp takes you straight to that answer in the recording.

@[Stephen Epathite after the penalty shootout at Juizo FC](/assets/audio/stephen-juizo-reaction.mp3#3:11|/assets/players/stephen-epathite-portrait.webp)

> 1:00 A goal. A goal. One-nil would have done it.

?? 0:07 | Disciplined, and half a plan | A disappointing way to exit the competition, particularly after holding a side four divisions above us to a goalless draw. What was your overall assessment of today's performance?

I am happy and I am frustrated at the same time.

Defensively, the whole team were very disciplined. Off the ball they were disciplined and they executed what I wanted from the start, which was a clean sheet, which was to keep them out, which was to frustrate them, which was to make them play long balls over the top, which I knew that Luke and the players in front of him could deal with.

And the plan genuinely was to win the game one or two nil. We executed half of that plan and not the other half.

++[26/27]

?? 0:49 | Just a goal | We came into today's game having scored 24 goals in five games, but for one reason or another we could not find a breakthrough this time. What do you feel was missing from our attacking play today?

A goal. A goal. One-nil would have done it. We were comfortable defensively.

Luke pulled off an outstanding save, which he usually does, but I thought we were comfortable defensively.

We need to make sure that we are scoring goals in important situations. Set pieces, open play, chances that we get. That is what was missing today, just a goal.

?? 1:25 | The message afterwards | After ninety minutes of hard work, to go out on penalties is obviously difficult to take. What was your message to the boys after the game?

It is a shit one, going out on penalties.

The message at the end was pretty much what I said about being frustrated that we could not win the game in ninety minutes, which I thought we were good for. Obviously we did not score the goal, so we were not. But I think a lot of the players felt frustrated that we did not win the game in ninety minutes.

And the message was that I was proud of them. When a team executes something that you want as a manager or a coach, you always feel happy, and you always feel happy that they have listened and taken the responsibility to do that, which I was really happy with.

As I said, it was just the goal that was missing.

?? 2:18 | Another way to score | Finally, we have got plenty to play for this season, including another cup tie against Celtic Swans, which has already been confirmed, but we are just waiting for a date. How do we make sure we take lessons from today and come back stronger?

The lessons from today would be that defensively I thought we were fine. We had enough firepower through the back and the middle to keep clean sheets and keep teams out.

But we need to find other ways of scoring if our strikers on the day cannot find that goal. We need to find goals from set pieces, which we did last year. We found goals from set pieces from different players, which was very effective.

So the message will be the same. It will be that we have to be hard to beat, and when we get a chance in front of goal we have to take it. That will be the difference.

## What is left

The Brian Howard President's Cup tie at home to Celtic Swans FC is confirmed, with the date still to be set.

League Eight returns on Sunday 1 November, at The Reeves Sports Club against TSM Rovers, 11:00.
